catalog_quote: 撒奇萊雅語的重音，大都落在詞最後一個音節上的元音，故通常不須標出。當詞根或詞幹加上詞綴時，重音跟著移動，因此重音會落在新詞的最後一個音節上，例如表2.6所示：[表2.6 撒奇萊雅語重音位置: 詞根 kan [kan]「吃」; 加綴 mu- → 新詞 mukan [mukán]「在吃」; -en → kanen [kanə́n]「將吃」; -an → kanan [kanán]「吃了」] 只有表示強調或在疑問句時，重音才有可能落在詞的倒數第二音節。例如：nacilá「昨天」重音在la；而i nacíla表示「昨天的昨天」，即是「前天」的意思，則重音向前移至倒數第二個音節ci；此外，iza表示可以看見的「那裡」，yíza表示「更遠看不見的遠方」，重音會往前移到ya。疑問句重音部分留待第十一章再作詳述。 [Shen 2018 p. 17] ... Declaratives serve as a phonetic baseline, where word stress in lexical isolation is consistently realized with word-final prominence. [Khuat 2026 p. 318] ... In AM terms, stress in Sakizaya surfaces as H* Lω (Figure 1), yielding a consistent word-final fall [p. 319] ... The stress-shift analysis is disfavored because isolated forms consistently retain ultimate prominence. [p. 320]

All three spliced passages are verbatim at the stated locators: p. 318 Abstract 'Declaratives serve as a phonetic baseline, where word stress in lexical isolation is consistently realized with word-final prominence.'; p. 319 sec. 3.1 'In AM terms, stress in Sakizaya surfaces as H* L[omega] (Figure 1), yielding a consistent word-final fall, whereas in Falangaw Amis, stress is realized as H* L%, producing a full falling contour only in sentence-fi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word (ultimate stress), phonetically a high pitch target on the final syllable followed by a fall (an L boundary tone at the right edge of the prosodic word); the final-syllable prominence stays put across sentence types (declaratives, wh-questions, imperatives). Affixation moves stress to the new final syllable (reported from Shen 2018 p. 17 and earlier Amis sources).
new_statements.exceptions: Function words, even disyllabic ones, are not stress-bearing units and cliticize rightward to the following prosodic word (sec. 3.2, p. 319, citing Chen 1987 p. 17); sentence-level high tone can surface on post-verbal imperative clitics without moving the lexical word's ultimate prominence (sec. 5); the penultimate high tone found in Falangaw Amis wh-questions is absent in Sakizaya. Affixation-triggered stress reassignment is cited second-hand (Shen 2018 p. 17; Ho 2008 ch. 4; Tsukida 1993; Edmondson & Huang 2004).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: content words in lexical isolation (citation forms) recorded from Sakizaya speakers in northern Hualien; the prosodic word (H* L-omega) is the stress domain, and the same ultimate prominence is verified inside declarative, wh-interrogative and imperative sentences. Sentence-level nuclear accent is separately described in Chen, Shen, Sung & Fon 2008 (default on the last syllable of the sentence, shifting to the penult in yes/no questions and exclamations).
new_statements.identity_note: Khuat 2026 treats Sakizaya as a variety closely related to (Northern/Nataoran) Amis and records its own Sakizaya speakers in northern Hualien, i.e. the language of Glottolog saki1247; the paper's parallel Falangaw Amis data (Taitung) belong to amis1246 and are not used for the statement. The general Amis stress literature it cites (Chen 1987 Nataoran, Edmondson & Huang 2004 Hsiukuluan, Li 1982 Mavuakay) describes other Amis dialects.

new_statements.quote: 撒奇萊雅語的重音，大都落在詞最後一個音節上的元音，故通常不須標出。當詞根或詞幹加上詞綴時，重音跟著移動，因此重音會落在新詞的最後一個音節上，例如表2.6所示：[表2.6: kan [kan]「吃」; mu- → mukan [mukán]「在吃」; -en → kanen [kanə́n]「將吃」; -an → kanan [kanán]「吃了」] 只有表示強調或在疑問句時，重音才有可能落在詞的倒數第二音節。例如：nacilá「昨天」重音在la；而i nacíla表示「昨天的昨天」，即是「前天」的意思，則重音向前移至倒數第二個音節ci；此外，iza表示可以看見的「那裡」，yíza表示「更遠看不見的遠方」，重音會往前移到ya。疑問句重音部分留待第十一章再作詳述。 [p. 17]
new_statements.translation: Stress in Sakizaya mostly falls on the vowel of the last syllable of the word, so it normally need not be marked. When a root or stem takes an affix, the stress moves along with it, so the stress falls on the last syllable of the new word, as shown in Table 2.6: [kan 'eat'; mu- → mukan [mukán] 'is eating'; -en → kanen [kanə́n] 'will eat'; -an → kanan [kanán] 'ate']. Only for emphasis or in interrogative sentences can the stress fall on the penultimate syllable of the word. For example, nacilá 'yesterday' has stress on la, whereas i nacíla means 'the yesterday of yesterday', i.e. 'the day before yesterday', with the stress moved forward to the penultimate syllable ci; likewise iza means a visible 'there', and yíza means 'a farther place out of sight', with the stress moved forward to ya. Stress in interrogatives is treated in detail in Chapter 11. [p. 17]

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (final syllable) and as Khuat 2026 (word-final prominence, H* Lω); adds the morphological detail that stress re-aligns to the final syllable of the affixed word, the emphasis/lexical penult cases, the yes/no-question penult shift, and unstressed-schwa deletion. Khuat 2026 cites this very page ('[8, p.17]').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word, and it shifts to the new final syllable when suffixes are added (kan → kanén, kanán; prefixed mukán). Penultimate stress is marginal: it occurs only for emphasis, in a few lexicalized contrasts (nacilá 'yesterday' vs i nacíla 'day before yesterday'; iza vs yíza), and in yes/no questions, where the sentence-final word takes penultimate stress instead (sec. 4.1.4 p. 44: tubáh in a statement vs túbah in the question; sec. 11.1 pp. 119-120: 句子的重音落在最後一字的倒數第二個音節元音上, e.g. ciníza? vs cinizá). Unstressed e /ə/ is often deleted (p. 18, rule 2).
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate stress for emphasis and in a few lexical pairs (nacilá vs i nacíla; iza vs yíza); in yes/no questions without a question particle the last word of the sentence is stressed on the penult (pp. 44, 119-120); with a question particle (haw/saw/hakya) the sentence stress falls on the final vowel of the penultimate word (p. 119).
new_statements.identity_note: Shen 2018 describes Sakizaya generally (Council of Indigenous Peoples reference grammar; no dialect named). Macaulay 2021 per its abstract covers Amis (a distinct Glottolog language) and 12 other Formosan languages, not Sakizaya.

sources.note: Instrumental study with Sakizaya data recorded in northern Hualien: word stress in lexical isolation is consistently word-final (ultimate), realized as H* plus a low boundary tone at the right edge of the prosodic word (a word-final fall); ultimate prominence is retained in wh-questions and imperatives; function words (even disyllabic) are not stress-bearing and lean rightward; affixation reassigns stress to the new final syllable (reported second-hand from Shen 2018 p. 17, Tsukida 1993, Edmondson & Huang 2004).
